title: Dysphagia: A Practical Approach
subtitle: Localize the problem, identify the pattern & choose the next test

sections.heading: Localize first
items: Oropharyngeal: difficulty initiating swallow, coughing, drooling or nasal regurgitation.
Esophageal: sensation of food sticking after swallowing; evaluate with EGD ± barium swallow.

sections.heading: Use the food pattern
items: Solids > liquids suggests structural disease: rings/webs, stricture, eosinophilic esophagitis or cancer.
Solids + liquids suggests a motility disorder; if endoscopy is unrevealing, proceed to manometry.

sections.heading: Motility clues
items: Intermittent symptoms ± chest pain: consider distal esophageal spasm or hypercontractile esophagus.
Progressive dysphagia: consider achalasia; hypomotility can occur with systemic disease.

sections.heading: Eosinophilic esophagitis — 2025 ACG
items: Diagnosis: esophageal dysfunction + ≥15 eos/hpf on biopsy, after evaluating other causes.
First line: shared decision-making—PPI, swallowed topical steroid, or empiric elimination diet.
If diet chosen, start less restrictive (1-FED or 2-FED); assess response with endoscopy + biopsy.

callout: Food impaction or progressive dysphagia warrants prompt evaluation; dilation does not replace anti-inflammatory EoE therapy.
